messages:
Jon (Customer): Hey team — we're seeing a bunch of streaming responses from your API that cut off mid-output. Client sees partial JSON, then the connection closes. Happens after ~20s on larger responses. Not consistent but frequent. We tried reconnects and sometimes get a 401 on the next request which makes debugging annoying.

Alisha (Support): sorry to hear that, thanks for reporting. can you paste the client-side code you're using to consume SSE, and any server request ids/response ids you see? also which region + model?

Jon (Customer): Node fetch to read body as stream, gist:
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  // process chunk
  await heavyProcessing(value); // simulating slow consumer
}
```
We're on hosted-us-east, model: rwd-13b-instruct. Tokens ~2000.

Alisha (Support): thanks. two quick asks: 1) can you reproduce with a minimal harness that just reads slowly (add a sleep between reads) and 2) can you share request id from the response headers (x-request-id or similar) when it happens?

Jon (Customer): repro attached — I slowed consumer to 150ms per chunk and it reproduces reliably. sample request-id: x-rid: 01GF7Z3KX0

sre-bot: Incident note: multiple streaming sessions for request 01GF7Z3KX0 logged write errors: [EAGAIN, EPIPE] in proxy layer. Tags: slow-consumer, proxy-buffering, partial-chunk.

Ben (Infra): pinging infra. initial guess: client is too slow draining socket, kernel send buffer fills, attempts to write hit EAGAIN and eventually upstream aborts. check proxy (nginx) proxy_buffering settings and keepalive timeouts. also need to see app logs for `short write`/`broken pipe`.

Maya (Eng): can you share the raw server logs around 01GF7Z3KX0? any traces of grpc/send loop errors?

Jon (Customer): pasted logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:01Z] INFO stream-start request=01GF7Z3KX0 model=rwd-13b-instruct
[2026-03-12T14:02:21Z] ERROR write failed: write /proc/xyz EAGAIN
[2026-03-12T14:02:22Z] WARN client stalled, aborting stream request=01GF7Z3KX0
[2026-03-12T14:02:22Z] INFO connection closed by server
```
And on a few reconnects we see a 401 on the subsequent POST within ~5s of stream end. not sure if that's related.

Ben (Infra): that log matches slow-consumer socket pressure. two likely contributors: 1) a proxy (nginx) is buffering and then hitting backlog limits; 2) our runtime's write loop doesn't block politely and will abort when kernel refuses. For the 401s — those could be token refresh race on your client or our auth cache expiring on reconnects. please confirm if you're rotating tokens between connections.

Jon (Customer): we do refresh tokens occasionally using an auth server. but in repro I used a long-lived test token so shouldn't hit 401. seems separate.

Maya (Eng): repro steps we ran in dev env: run a simple SSE server that writes 32KB every 50ms. run a client that reads but sleeps 200ms between chunks. we saw the server hitting EAGAIN -> EPIPE after ~18s and then the app closed the FD. sample strace snippet:
```
write(3, "<chunk>", 32768) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
write(3, "<chunk>", 32768) = -1 EPIPE (Broken pipe)
```
Also saw nginx upstream logs with `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `client timed out while reading response header`.

Alisha (Support): ok good repro. for a short-term workaround: 1) disable proxy buffering (proxy_buffering off; proxy_max_temp_file_size 0) or set smaller proxy_buffers, 2) send smaller chunks or add `flush()` after every chunk from server, 3) have client read more often (reduce processing on main thread or offload). can you try disabling buffering on your side if you have a proxy?

Jon (Customer): disabling proxy buffering wasn't an option (we're using managed infra). we tried increasing client read concurrency (processing chunks in worker threads) and it mitigated but not eliminated the issue.

Ben (Infra): longer-term we should implement backpressure-aware write path in runtime: if kernel returns EAGAIN, we should slow the send attempt and yield rather than immediately abort. also consider a bounded per-client send queue and drop/connect with an informative SSE event instead of silent close. I'll open an eng runtime ticket.

Maya (Eng): additional suggestions: add periodic SSE pings (comments or `:keepalive

`) to keep the connection active in proxies, and implement `last-event-id` handling so clients can resume after reconnect without losing complete semantics. also ensure we set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` so intermediaries don't buffer.

Jon (Customer): what about the partial JSON problem? clients get truncated JSON and then can't recover.

Alisha (Support): we recommend streaming line-delimited JSON objects (`\n` delimited) and ensuring server always emits a well-formed final event like `event: done\ndata: {"status":"aborted","reason":"slow_consumer"}\n\n` so client-side can detect incomplete stream and retry using `last-event-id`. we'll also add guidance to docs.

sre-bot: Escalation created: REQ-1102 -> eng-runtime. Priority: P2. Owner: Ben. Includes repro harness and strace output.

Ben (Infra): next steps for us: 1) eng-runtime to add graceful backoff on EAGAIN instead of immediate abort, 2) add a server-side metric for `stream_write_eagain` and alert if > threshold, 3) docs/SDK sample showing reconnect with last-event-id and defensive parsing.

Maya (Eng): quick mitigation we can deploy in a patch: catch `EAGAIN` in send loop, do an exponential backoff up to 1s, then if still failing emit final event and close gracefully. I'll PR this today to a canary pool.

Alisha (Support): Jon — will keep you updated on the PR and canary results. in the meantime please share any examples of the 401 after reconnect; if you see it again include the request id and full headers.

Jon (Customer): thanks — we'll try the worker-thread approach for processing and will capture the 401 traces when they happen. appreciate the fast response. :thumbsup:

Alisha (Support): np. marking this thread as incident-linked and escalating. will follow up when eng gives canary ETA.

Ben (Infra): action items assigned: Ben -> open REQ-1102 (done), Maya -> patch backoff behavior (in progress), Alisha -> collect more customer traces and confirm 401 repro (waiting).

Jon (Customer): quick note: I ran tcpdump during repro, and saw zero retransmits until the server closed, so looks like application-level close not network flakiness. sharing pcap on request.

Alisha (Support): got it. thank you — we'll update here once the canary is out and if you want we can join a short debug session to reproduce live.

Maya (Eng): PR opened: r/inference/runtime#452. patch implements EAGAIN backoff + final event on abort. rolling to canary group 2.

sre-bot: Canary deployment started for PR r/inference/runtime#452. Canary IDs: c-9c12, c-9c13. Monitoring stream_write_eagain metric.

Alisha (Support): thanks everyone. Jon — will ping when canary passes or if we need logs. feel free to DM if you want a live repro session.

Jon (Customer): thanks all, appreciate the help.
